sources.entry: Adrafinil - Keeps your Mac awake only while AI agents are working, then lets it sleep normally.

summary.one_liner: Adrafinil is a macOS menubar app that keeps a closed-lid Mac awake while AI coding agents are working and releases the hold when the turn ends.
summary.what_it_does: It uses hooks to track active agent work across multiple coding agents, holding the Mac awake per session and resuming normal sleep after the last hold ends. It lists hook support for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Devin, Aider, Hermes, OpenCode, Cline, and Pi. Closed-lid sleep control runs through a privileged helper. Safety limits include a thermal cutout and automatic release of abandoned holds, and timed holds and a manual "Let it sleep" control are available. It also offers a CLI and MCP access, optional detection of running agent processes, lid-close audio confirmation, and a lid-open activity/temperature summary. An opt-in anonymous check-in is described in the README, which says nothing is sent unless the user agrees.
use_cases: keep a MacBook awake with lid closed during long agent runs
prevent sleep while Claude Code or Codex is working
release sleep automatically when an AI agent finishes
limit unattended coding agent sessions with thermal protection
manage overlapping agent sessions on one Mac
notable: Per-session acquire/release so overlapping agents each hold the Mac awake independently
Thermal cutout and automatic release of abandoned holds for unattended runs
Hooks integrate with about ten named coding agents
Opt-in anonymous check-in with documented deletion on opt-out
caveats: Requires macOS 26.4+ (macOS 15 backport mentioned without details)
Administrator approval needed for the privileged helper
Agent hooks must be installed manually in Settings
